findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on missing, unreadable, or untrusted file paths.
findings.failure_mode: External file path causes process abort instead of returning a typed I/O error.
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> and use fs::read_to_string(path)? or .map_err(io::Error::custom) without unwrap.

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric or out-of-range field values.
findings.failure_mode: Malformed CSV value crashes the process instead of returning a typed parse error.
findings.fix: Use .map_err(...) or ? to propagate ParseError, and return Result<Vec<Record>, E> with a domain or io error type.

findings.problem: parts is indexed at [0] and [1] without bounds checking. Lines with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields cause a panic.
findings.failure_mode: Truncated or single-field CSV lines panic at runtime.
findings.fix: Use parts.first() and parts.get(1) and handle None with map_err or return a typed malformed-line error.

findings.problem: parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 silently truncates values above 65535.
findings.failure_mode: Values in [65536, u32::MAX] wrap around, producing invalid Record data without any indication of overflow.
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap()) or better parse directly as u16 (parts[1].parse::<u16>()) and propagate errors.

findings.problem: println!() inside load_audits is a hidden I/O side effect in a function that should be pure parsing logic.
findings.failure_mode: Logging is embedded in the data-parsing pipeline, making it impossible to test parsing deterministically and mixing shell concerns with core concerns.
findings.fix: Move println! to the caller/shell layer. load_audits should return parsed records without side effects. If audit logging is needed, pass a writer or callback abstraction.

findings.problem: load_audits mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string) with parsing logic in a single public function. No functional core / imperative shell split.
findings.failure_mode: Cannot unit-test parsing without mocking the filesystem; parsing logic is not independently verifiable or deterministic.
findings.fix: Split into (1) load_audits_raw(path: &str) -> Result<String, io::Error> for I/O and (2) parse_records(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> for pure logic. Call parse_records from load_audits_raw.

findings.problem: collect() into Vec<String> allocates an intermediate heap collection for every line, even when only 2 fields are needed.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocations per line increase allocation pressure and allocation-count variance in tight loops.
findings.fix: Use split_once(',', line).map(...) or iterator-based splitting with take(2) to avoid Vec allocation per line.

Multiple BLOCKERs remain: unwrap on fallible I/O and parse, lossy u32-to-u16 cast, unchecked indexing on split results, hidden println side effect in core logic, and no functional core/shell separation.
